canonical_data: Locally stored sessions linked to their project, holding tool calls, permission decisions, goals, model configuration and verification evidence, plus project and personal skill and memory files
current_repo_note: Covers the DeepCode coding agent as it stands in this repository, whose README now leads with an engineering agent and keeps Paper2Code, its original paper-to-code direction, as a dedicated workflow. Older descriptions and the arXiv paper describe the earlier multi-agent Paper2Code architecture. The bundled pinned skills carry their own Apache-2.0 licence files while the application is MIT. README re-read 2026-10-10: the MIT licence blob is unchanged and no scope statement moved.
strengths: Execution is a stated product boundary: every project needs explicit trust, a tool call resumes exactly where an approval suspended it, and crash recovery settles incomplete turns without replaying side effects
Completion is judged against evidence the task selects, such as tests, builds, diagnostics, and diffs, and a failed check feeds the next repair rather than ending as success
Clients share one local service and session store, so a goal started in the terminal can be continued in the desktop app after a restart or a model switch
weaknesses: The README has been rewritten around a new engineering-agent architecture while the arXiv paper and older documentation describe a different Paper2Code design, so published results do not describe the current code
The Full access mode removes approval and filesystem sandbox boundaries once a person confirms it for a session
Much of the product is new relative to the repository's age, with the verification and loop claims resting on the maintainers' own documentation and tests
why_it_matters: A fast-growing academic-lab project that has been rebuilt from a paper-reproduction pipeline into a permissioned, verifying coding agent, giving a local-first option with an explicit evidence-based definition of done.
